name: Lowell Observatory
description: An astronomical research center from which the dwarf planet Pluto was discovered, this historic institution is on a mesa overlooking the west side of town. The staff leads guided daytime tours, and visitors use the Observatory's 24" Clark telescope and smaller portable telescopes during regular…

name: Museum of Northern Arizona
description: On the north side of town, it has displays on Native American life and the natural history of the region. A good selection of Native American folk art, particularly Navajo rugs, is available at the gift shop.

name: Arboretum at Flagstaff
description: This 200-acre botanical garden, environmental research station, and nature center displays one of America's largest collections of high country wildflowers. Daily guided tours at 11AM and 1PM. Wild Birds of Prey programs at F-M noon and 2PM.

name: Riordan Mansion State Historic Park
description: This fine example of an Arts and Crafts style house was built in 1904 for a prominent local family. Guided tours are conducted at the top of the hour, reservations recommended.

name: Pioneer Museum
description: This small state museum collects, preserves and exhibits artifacts, documents and photographs of the history of Flagstaff and northern Arizona. It also hosts a number of events throughout the year.

name: Fort Tuthill Military Museum
description: A former National Guard training facility built in 1929, this small museum now has displays devoted to regional military history.
price: $3 (adults 13+), Free (seniors, children, active military, National Guard members)
hours: May-Sep: Thu Fri noon-4PM (based on staff availability), Sat Sun 10AM-4PM

name: Northern Arizona University Art Museum
description: Has rotating exhibits featuring local and international artists.
hours: Tue-Sat noon-5PM during the school year

name: Coconino Center for the Arts
description: The largest gallery in northern Arizona, showcases local and regional art.

name: Elden Pueblo Historic Site
description: A Sinagua archeological site which was inhabited from 1050-1275 CE. An easy interpretive trail circles the ruins. It is managed by the Coconino National Forest Service, which hosts a number of educational programs and workshops at the site.

name: Picture Canyon Natural and Cultural Preserve
Absolute Bikes
description: Mountain bikes can be rented

name: Mount Elden
description: This area is managed by the Coconino National Forest, and is an excellent starting point for exploring the area with numerous trails running up and alongside most faces of the mountain. One of the most popular trails is Elden Lookout Trail , which scales all 2800 ft (855m) from base to summit, and…

name: San Francisco Peaks
description: Managed by the Coconino National Forest, the San Francisco Peaks northwest of Flagstaff offer a number of hiking trails for all skill levels, as well as opportunities for mountain biking, rock climbing, camping, and skiing. The range is crowned by the 12,637-ft Humphreys Peak, and is held sacred by…

name: Arizona Snowbowl
description: Alpine skiing. One of only three ski resorts in the state of Arizona. Despite the surrounding desert, Flagstaff is a popular skiing destination for the Southwest due to the high elevation. Interestingly, the Snowbowl is one of the first ten ski resorts established in the United States. Snowbowl is…

name: Flagstaff Nordic Center
description: One of the southwest's best cross-country skiing areas with over 50 km of well-groom ski trails and 25 km of snowshoe trails. In the summer the trails are open for hiking and mountain biking. Trail passes and equipment rental prices are listed here ; overnight cabin rental is also available.

name: Jay Lively Activity Center
description: City-owned permanent indoor ice skating rink. Offers ice skating lessons, public skating sessions, and also hosts ice hockey games.

name: Northern Arizona Yoga Center
description: Northern Arizona Yoga Center is the largest yoga studio in town. This studio offers more than just yoga: they also host Salsa parties, Tango classes, Capoiera, Pilates, and Tai Chi. They are also a great supplier of yoga clothing and accessories. They are partners with the Vertical Relief Climbing…

name: Flagstaff Extreme Adventure Course
description: A suspended obstacle course with more than 70 aerial challenges for children and adults.

name: Hitchin’ Post Stables
description: Offers guided horseback riding excursions forest land southeast of Flagstaff, ranging from 1 to 8 hours in length.

name: First Friday ArtWalk
description: Every first Friday of the month art galleries and restaurants stay open until late in the evening, with live street entertainment and music centered around Heritage Square.

name: Zuni Festival of Arts and Culture
description: Held annually in late May, this two-day festival sponsored by NAU celebrates Zuni culture with dance and music, and arts and crafts demonstrations and exhibits.

name: Hopi Festival of Arts and Culture
description: Held annually around the third week of August, this festival celebrates Hopi traditions and culture with music, dance, food, and arts and crafts exhibits.

name: Navajo Festival of Arts and Culture
description: Held annually in early August, celebrates Diné (Navajo) culture with music, dance, lectures, food, art, and weaving demonstrations.

name: Celebraciones de la Gente
description: Held in late October, this festival celebrates the Mexican holiday Dia de los Muertos, or Day of the Dead . Activities include mariachi music, storytelling, and arts demonstrations. Ofrendas (private altars) are exhibited in the courtyard.

name: Arizona Highland Celtic Festival
description: Held every July, with music, dance, and food and drink.

name: Pickin' in the Pines Bluegrass & Acoustic Music Festival
description: Held annually in mid-September.

name: Coconino County Fair
description: Held annually in September and features traditional fair exhibits, entertainment, livestock auctions, and carnival rides.

name: Dara Thai Restaurant
description: Downtown, centrally located serving decent Thai food. Get a seat by the window and view San Francisco Street while you dine. Takeout available.

name: Hunan East
description: Great Chinese food in a casual atmosphere. Takeout available.

name: Little Thai Kitchen
description: A Thai restaurant popular with locals.

name: Pato Thai
description: Downtown, another popular one with locals.

name: Fratelli Pizza
description: A pizza place that is well-loved by the locals. They have cheese, pepperoni, and pesto slices, and many specialty pies. Their pizza is hand-tossed, thin crust, brick oven pizza, like what is found back east.

name: New Jersey Pizza Company
description: Excellent choice for those looking for an all organic menu or more exotic options than the typical pizza restaurant offers.

name: NiMarcos Pizza
description: Locally owned and operated in Flagstaff for years, NiMarcos offers semi-thick crust pizza, salads and soft-serve ice cream. Go in and order your own pie or just buy a slice. Local favorite.

name: Oregano's Pizza Bistro
description: Fantastic Chicago-style pizza with a great throw-back atmosphere.

name: Pizzicletta
description: A Neapolitan style pizza place with house-made gelato. Takeout available. You can sit next door at Mother Road Brewery and order from Pizzicleta next door.

name: La Fonda Mexican Restaurant
description: Same location since the 1950s, this a well-loved Mexican restaurant with great salsa and authentic dishes. Is busy most times so expect to wait to be seated.

name: MartAnne's Cafe
description: Mexican breakfast/brunch. Awesome food, huge portions at fairly reasonable prices. Cash only.

name: Bigfoot BBQ
description: This is the place to go if you have a hankering for a pulled pork sandwich or a batch of fried okra. They even serve gourmet hotdogs. Owned by a Georgia native turned Flagstaff resident, you won't want to miss out on this!

name: Brandy's Restaurant & Bakery
description: Breakfast features quiche of the day, seven grain French toast, specialty egg dishes, homemade pastries and many other quality items. Lunch features tons of tasty sandwiches and burgers. Dinner is slightly more upscale but definitely affordable ($10-15 a plate) and features the wonderful creations…

name: Charly's Pub & Grill
description: Live blues music in the evening.

name: Diablo Burger
description: Although tricky to find and seating is rather limited, this place is one of those extraordinarily rewarding discoveries for the persistent traveler. Their burgers ($8-10) are made from range-raised beef from a ranch just north of Flagstaff, served on an English muffin with a boatload of…

name: Macy's European Coffeehouse
description: They roast their own coffee and have lots of vegan foodstuffs. A favorite amongst the hippies.

name: Silver Pine Restaurant
description: The Silver Pine Restaurant is one of Flagstaff's most popular dining choices, American cuisine.
hours: Daily for breakfast, lunch and dinner

name: Fry's
description: Has a full-service hot and cold deli, and onsite pharmacy.

name: DuBeau Hostel
description: Free wi-fi and breakfast, free coffee and tea available throughout the day.

name: Grand Canyon International Hostel
description: Free wi-fi and breakfast, free coffee and tea available throughout the day.

name: Hotel Monte Vista
description: Stay at the same hotel where some scenes of Casablanca were shot. Opened in 1927, the hotel hosted such illustrious guests as Bing Crospy, Spencer Tracy, and Jane Russell, and is widely reputed to be haunted.

name: Sleep Inn
description: 58-room hotel. Non-smoking, free breakfast and wi-fi, pets welcome. Indoor pool.

name: Weatherford Hotel
description: Noted novelist Zane Grey wrote Call of the Canyon while staying here. Widely rumored to be haunted.

name: Days Inn and Suites East Flagstaff
description: Pet-friendly lodging with king-size beds, which also provides a complimentary deluxe continental breakfast.

name: Starlight Pines Bed & Breakfast
description: 1912 Victorian style B/B. Four guest rooms with private baths, Lily with private balcony overlooking Mount Elden, Dragonfly with wood-burning fireplace.

name: England House Bed and Breakfast
description: This well-respected bed and breakfast is just four blocks from Flagstaff's historic downtown. England house was built in the early 1900s and is now furnished with antiques from the late 1800s. Breakfast is served on the bright sun porch.

name: Little America Hotel Flagstaff
description: Antique, continental flair. One of the more unique hotel experiences that Flagstaff has to offer. Free airport shuttle from 7AM-10PM.

name: Flagstaff Rental Cabin
description: 3-bedroom cabin with two king size fully adjustable beds with massage upstairs and two queen beds downstairs. Ralph Lauren bedding throughout. 55" 3D TV and fireplace in the great room.

name: Bonito Campground
description: Open beginning of May to mid-October. This campground with 44 sites is very popular and is close to Wupatki and Sunset Crater National Monuments. Drinking water, flush toilets, no hookups, trailers/RVs under 42'.

name: Canyon Vista Campground
description: Open beginning of May to mid-October, with 11 individual sites. Located near Walnut Canyon, with good views of the San Francisco Peaks. Drinking water and vault toilets, no hookups, trailers/RVs under 22'.

name: Fort Tuthill County Park Campground
description: Facilities include a few hook-up sites, picnic tables, fire rings, portable toilets, and water spigots. No water or electricity available. Reservations can be made by phone or online .

name: Lockett Meadow Campground
description: Open mid-May to mid-September, with 17 individual sites. A very popular campground with great views of the San Francisco Peaks. No water, vault toilets. Not recommended for trailers/RVs.

name: Fernow Cabin
description: A retired US Forest Service Fire Guard Station, this 3-BR log cabin housed fire fighters in the summer. The cabin can sleep up to 8 people, and is furnished with bunks, stove, and pots and pans, and vault toilet. Campers must bring their own bedding supplies. Open April 15 - November 15…

name: Kendrick Cabin
description: A retired US Forest Service Fire Guard Station, this 3-BR stone-built cabin housed fire fighters in the summer. Can sleep up to 10 people and is furnished with bunks, stove, and pots and pans; there is an outside bath house with flush toilet and shower. Campers must bring their own bedding…

name: Arizona Nordic Village
description: Offers yurts and log-sided camper cabins to rent. Yurts and cabins have bunks or mattress pads and wood stoves; no electricity or water. Wi-fi and showers are available at the main lodge, which also offers mountain bikes for rent. Reservations can be made by phone or online.

name: Flagstaff KOA
description: Spaces for trailers/RVs and tents, cabins available. Laundry, showers, wi-fi and shuttle bus; bicycles available to rent.

name: Black Barts RV Park / Steakhouse & Saloon
description: Full hookups with 50-amp service.
